Author: Kuldeep Mathur Bench: Kuldeep Mathur [2024:RJ-JD:13596]
 HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR  S.B. Criminal Revision Petition No. 981/2002 Fatehlal S/o Mohanlalji Kumawat, resident of Sanwad, Police Station Rajnagar, District Rajsamand. (At present lodged in Rajsamand Jail.)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State of Rajasthan  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. R.S. Chundawat

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT  JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr. Mahipal Bishnoi, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR  ORDER 20/03/2024

By way of filing the present revision petition, the revisionist- petitioner has challenged the order dated 12.02.1999 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajsamand in Criminal Regular Case No.104/1996 whereby the learned Chief judicial Magistrate has convicted and sentenced the petitioner for the offence under Sections 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and the order dated 31.10.2002 passed by the learned Additional Session Judge (Fast Track),
Rajsamand in Criminal Appeal No.81/2002 whereby the judgment of the learned trial Court has been upheld.
As per the prosecution, on 15.03.1996, certain milk samples were taken from two drums in possession of the petitioner who is a milk vendor.

The report of the milk samples prepared by the public analyst, Jaipur, in conformity with the procedure provided under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act revealed that the milk [2024:RJ-JD:13596] (2 of 4) [CRLR-981/2002] found in the possession of the petitioner was 'Adulterated'.
The petitioner was thereafter prosecuted for the offence under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced as above.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.

There is no positive evidence available on record indicating that the petitioner is guilty Fatehlal vs State (2024:Rj-Jd:13596) on 20 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26815335/
1 of committing the alleged crime.
Learned counsel vehemently submitted that as a matter of fact, the milk was not for general sale but the same was being taken to the factory where the petitioner was a supervisor, for a tea party.

Learned counsel further submitted that merely on the basis of the report of public analyst, it cannot be said that the petitioner had committed the alleged crime or that the milk was 'adulterated'.
Lastly, on the strength of the aforesaid arguments and the facts and circumstances of the above case,
learned counsel submitted that since the incident in the present case relates to the year 1996 and since the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents, therefore, the present revision petition deserves acceptance.
Learned counsel for the petitioner in the alternative submitted that the occurrence relates to the year 1996 and the petitioner has already served some part of the sentence awarded to him,
therefore, the substantive sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
[2024:RJ-JD:13596] (3 of 4) [CRLR-981/2002] Reliance was placed on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:
2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623 and a judgment of the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CrilLJ 2582.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that there is no illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgments whatsoever and therefore, the same do not call for any interference in exercise of revisional jurisdiction by this Court.

entities.text:
Puttaswamy v State of Karnataka:
2009 (1) WLC (SC) (Cri.) 623
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Kamla Prasad v. State of Rajasthan: 2014 CrilLJ 2582
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard.
A perusal of the impugned judgments makes it manifest that the alleged incident happened in the year 1996 and the revision petition is pending before this Court for adjudication since 2002.

The record of the case indicates that petitioner had already undergone detention for some period and since the case is pending before this Court since 2002, the petitioner had suffered both financial hardships and mental agony.

This Court finds that in the peculiar circumstances of the present case and looking to the nature of the offence committed by the revisionist-petitioner the alternative prayer that the sentence awarded to the present petitioner may be substituted with the period of sentence already undergone by him, deserves acceptance.
Accordingly, the revision petition is allowed.

While maintaining the conviction of the petitioner for the offence under section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the sentence awarded to him are reduced to the period already undergone by him.
